Forecast Discussion

High pressure is over the Ohio Valley today. It settles over the central Appalachians Tuesday and stays through Friday. That means sunshine, light wind, and afternoons that warm a little each day. Nights stay cold in valleys while the ridgetops remain rather mild.

Temperatures are above average for the second half of the workweek. Some high clouds arrive Thursday and Friday.

Saturday, the high moves to New England as low pressure develops off the Southeast coast. An easterly flow between the two brings clouds and cooler afternoons for the weekend. How close the low tracks to the coast decides the rest. At this point, I cannot rule out rain Saturday afternoon and evening. We should be able to be more specific on the potential for rain in a couple of days.

A cold front crosses Sunday night. I cannot rule out a shower Sunday afternoon or evening. Cooler air follows early next week.

Toward Thanksgiving, the weather looks cooler but not particularly cold.
